Thus, there is an urgent need to scale up the technologies for large-scale PFAS degradation. However, there are multiple challenges in transitioning the nanotechnologies to a larger scale. These include efficiency, toxicity assessment of nano - materials, their ultimate fate, recyclability, and reusability of nano - materials, in addition to cost-effectiveness. These methods concentrate PFAS, and end-of-life treatment technologies of concentrated waste streams become necessary. Several approaches for PFAS destruction have been proposed; among those are dual-frequency ultrasound (DFUS) [28] , plasma-based technology [29] , sonochemical destruction [30] , electro - chemical oxidation [7] , etc. These approaches can degrade PFAS, but they require long residence times, high energy consumption, and chemical additives such as sulfite, iodide, Fe(III), persulfate, or TiO 2 [31,32] . Hydrothermal treatment (HT) and supercritical water oxida - tion (SCWO) have been shown effective for the destruction of recalci - trant organic molecules and recently were investigated for PFAS treatment [33 – 35] . About 99 % PFOA and PFOS removal were achieved at T = 590 – 595 ◦ C, with residence times of 6 – 60 s. The remaining PFAS in the effluent consisted of mostly PFOS ( > 70 %); other compounds like PFHxS, PFBS, PFPeA, or PFOA were found in small amounts. About 62.6 % defluorination was measured, and the total fraction of short-chain PFAS increased from 3.8 % in the influent to 50.8 % in the effluent, indicating that long-chain PFAS were transformed into shorter-chain PFAS [61] . Since the details of the continuous flow SCWO reactors were not disclosed, it is not possible to evaluate the effect of operational parameters on PFAS decomposition or develop strategies for increasing PFAS mineralization. In the end, the plasma reactor performance is deter- mined by the types and amounts of reactive species that are available for reaction with the pollutants in the contaminated water. T ypes and amounts of reactive species in turn depend on the discharge type and plasma- feeding gas, but also on the reactor design and, most importantly , on the plasma/liquid interface, transport phenomena playing a crucial role.
